page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-16 is an Arm-based instance type positioned for memory-intensive workloads within the general-purpose family. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 architecture, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, accommodating applications that demand elevated RAM capacity relative to compute allocation without requiring specialized ultra-memory tiers.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage disks, requiring all non-volatile persistence to be handled via attached network storage volumes. Additionally, the instance features no discrete GPUs or specialized hardware accelerators, and offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Software stacks deployed to the instance must be compiled for the arm64 instruction set, which delivers standard integer and cryptographic execution paths without support for x86-specific advanced matrix or vector instruction sets.

With its 8:1 memory-to-core allocation, the n4a-highmem-16 provides cost-effective resource density for memory-bound tasks. The server is structured to support in-memory caching solutions, relational and document database servers, ETL pipelines, and container runtimes operating large resident datasets requiring predictable dedicated CPU execution.

Given its dedicated core allocation and elevated memory density, the n4a-highmem-16 is engineered for in-memory databases, distributed caching, memory-heavy data transformation pipelines, and enterprise application runtimes requiring dependable multi-core execution alongside large active working sets.
